sources.title: City of Bellevue - Work Requiring Permits
sources.supports: Siding replacement needs no permit except stucco and brick/stone veneer >4 ft above grade plane; installing/moving/widening exterior doors, skylights, windows needs permit with plan review; same-size same-location replacement needs none.

sources.title: Bellevue City Code 23.05.090 Permits required
sources.supports: Exemption for replacement of nonstructural siding on IRC structures except stucco and brick/stone veneer >4 ft; exemptions do not authorize code violations; one-code exemption does not exempt other technical codes; ordinary repairs exclude cutting structural beams/load-bearing supports.

sources.title: City of Bellevue - Residential Building Permits
sources.supports: Permit types BS/BR/BU/BT/BE; Earthquake Home Retrofit Program; Permit Center 425-452-4898, permits@bellevuewa.gov.

sources.title: City of Bellevue - Single-Family Remodel Permit (BU)
sources.supports: BU covers enlarging window/door openings, installing or relocating doorway headers, earthquake home retrofit; apply on MyBuildingPermit.

sources.title: City of Bellevue - Single-Family Remodel Permit, No Plan Review (BT)
sources.supports: Nonstructural work usually no plan review, same-day issuance; inspections required; inspector may require plans, plan review may involve three-week turnaround.

sources.title: Puget Sound Clean Air Agency - Homeowner Renovation
sources.supports: Owner-occupant may survey own single-family house for renovation; otherwise AHERA inspector; share results; friable removal needs Single-Family Residence Notification with a filing fee; renters/landlords/condos hire certified abatement contractor.

sources.title: Puget Sound Clean Air Agency - Asbestos
EPA - Lead Renovation, Repair and Painting Program
sources.supports: Anyone paid to disturb painted surfaces in pre-1978 homes must be certified, employees trained; generally does not apply to homeowners on own homes.

sources.title: Allura fiber cement installation manual
sources.supports: Flashing at window/door heads and horizontal penetrations sloped to drain; kickout flashing at roof-wall intersections.
